params.text: Enclosed by a double membrane (nuclear envelope) continuous with the rough ER. Nuclear pores control mRNA export and protein import. The nucleolus assembles ribosomal subunits. Contains the cell's DNA; DNA and RNA polymerases are its marker enzymes.

Two membranes: the outer is freely permeable via porins; the inner is impermeable, folded into cristae, and carries the electron transport chain and ATP synthase. The matrix holds TCA-cycle and β-oxidation enzymes plus circular mtDNA (maternally inherited). Mature red cells lack mitochondria, so glycolysis is their only ATP source. Marker: succinate dehydrogenase.

Single-membrane network studded with ribosomes. Synthesises secretory, membrane and lysosomal proteins and checks their folding — misfolded proteins are returned to the cytosol and destroyed by the proteasome (the quality-control process that retains misfolded F508del CFTR in cystic fibrosis and targets it for proteasomal degradation). Glucose-6-phosphatase marks the ER-derived microsomal fraction on centrifugation; it is not a marker that distinguishes rough from smooth ER.

Tubular membrane network without ribosomes. Synthesises phospholipids and steroid hormones; metabolises drugs via cytochrome P450 enzymes, which increase when drugs such as phenobarbital induce them. In muscle, the specialised smooth ER (sarcoplasmic reticulum) stores and releases calcium.

Stacked cisternae with a cis (receiving) and trans (shipping) face. Processes, glycosylates, sorts and packages proteins into vesicles bound for secretion, the plasma membrane or lysosomes. Marker: galactosyltransferase. In I-cell disease, the Golgi fails to tag lysosomal enzymes with mannose-6-phosphate, so they are secreted instead.

Single-membrane vesicle containing acid hydrolases that work at pH 4.5–5. Digests worn-out organelles (autophagy) and engulfed material. Marker: acid phosphatase. Deficiency of a single lysosomal enzyme causes a storage disease — Gaucher (glucocerebrosidase), Tay-Sachs (hexosaminidase A) or Niemann-Pick A/B (sphingomyelinase).
